description: I am a 2nd-year Electrical Engineering student specializing in DSP and machine learning. For this challenge, I am building AstroGuard: an edge-computing pipeline using Butterworth filters and PyTorch to detect and attribute astronaut physiological anomalies. I am tackling this hackathon as a strict solo participant to rigorously test my own end-to-end system design skills from scratch. Therefore, I am not looking for team members. Good luck!
summary:
High-Level Project Summary
During an EVA, if mission control receives a flood of telemetry alarms, every second counts. Is the anomaly a primary human cardiac event, a life-support suit failure, or just a disconnected sensor? AstroGuard is an edge-capable data pipeline that combines PyTorch deep learning with a deterministic logic script to instantly attribute the root cause of physiological anomalies without cloud-compute latency.Detailed Project Description
AstroGuard was engineered from scratch over 48 hours to prioritize strict edge-hardware constraints:Raw ECG Ingestion: 10-second overlapping sliding windows (7000 samples at 700Hz).Stateful Causal DSP: A 4th-order sosfilt Butterworth bandpass (0.5 - 50 Hz) removes baseline wander using strictly past data, ensuring true real-time viability.1D CNN Autoencoder: A PyTorch neural network, trained strictly on chronological physiological baselines, compresses the spatial features.99th-Percentile Thresholding: Reconstructions that deviate beyond the 99th percentile of the validation MSE trigger an anomaly flag.3-Way Attribution Logic: A deterministic agent cross-references the AI's MSE spikes with telemetry ($O_2$, $CO_2$, Impedance) to diagnose the root cause (Human vs. Suit vs. Sensor).
details:
AstroGuard was engineered from scratch over 48 hours to prioritize strict edge-hardware constraints:

  • Raw ECG Ingestion: 10-second overlapping sliding windows (7000 samples at 700Hz).
  • Stateful Causal DSP: A 4th-order sosfilt Butterworth bandpass (0.5 - 50 Hz) removes baseline wander using strictly past data, ensuring true real-time viability.
  • 1D CNN Autoencoder: A PyTorch neural network, trained strictly on chronological physiological baselines, compresses the spatial features.
  • 99th-Percentile Thresholding: Reconstructions that deviate beyond the 99th percentile of the validation MSE trigger an anomaly flag.
  • 3-Way Attribution Logic: A deterministic agent cross-references the AI's MSE spikes with telemetry ($O_2$, $CO_2$, Impedance) to diagnose the root cause (Human vs. Suit vs. Sensor).

Blind Benchmark Results: The model was evaluated on a strictly chronologically separated test block with randomized synthetic fault injections to prevent data leakage. It successfully diagnosed 100% of injected Sensor Faults (Impedance >10kOhm) and 100% of injected Suit Faults (Hypoxia / Amplitude Drop).

Limitations: The model is currently validated exclusively on WESAD Subject 2. Suit and sensor faults ($O_2$, $CO_2$, Impedance drops) were synthetically injected to test the attribution logic.

Space Agency Partner Data & References This project utilized physiological ECG baseline data from the WESAD (Wearable Stress and Affect Detection) dataset to train the neural network. Environmental suit telemetry was synthetically generated to simulate EVA conditions.
